_readme: Wisdom Loop authors (§2.1). Only these four author CALLs. Authorship is FIXED by this file, never inferred from voice or style.
Discord user IDs are verified by measured authorship of the author's own channel (GET /channels/{id}/messages?limit=50 with the bot token, 2026-09-13), not by display name.
Aliases normalise Zoom speaker labels, Discord display names, Substack section owners and X handles. Matching is case-insensitive and exact (no fuzzy matching).
A fifth regular author becomes role=candidate, flagged to the owner review queue, and is NOT ingested until ruled.
Bots and webhooks (e.g. the 'UCT Intelligence' webhook user 1527044971553620088 posting in #tsdr) are never authors.

ambiguous_speaker_labels.label: Uncharted Territory
ambiguous_speaker_labels.note: The shared Zoom host account label (owner ruling 2026-09-13, CONTRACTS §8a.2). Golden v1 found it carrying Bracco's voice in session 348, so it is NOT an alias of any author. Resolve per session ONLY with cited evidence (session title/description, a self-introduction line, a first-person reference to a position matching that author's Sunday Scans positions, or a Discord message by that author in the same minute), logged on the source record. Insufficient evidence -> speaker 'team-unresolved' (MENTION only; never CALL, never PRINCIPLE attribution) and an attribution review item. Never default to TSDR or Bracco; never voice similarity alone; never dropped as an attendee.

Owner ruling CONTRACTS §8a.2: resolve per session ONLY with cited evidence; with insufficient evidence the speaker is 'team-unresolved', which may author MENTION only — never CALL, never a PRINCIPLE attribution. single_token_aliases_reviewed._why: A single-token alphabetic alias is matched EXACTLY and case-insensitively against a Zoom display name, so if it is also a person's given name it silently attributes that person's words to a CALL author (reviewer finding F1, 2026-09-13). Every such alias must be listed here with a reason. tests/test_wisdom_authors_aliases.py fails BY NAME on any that is not — so the next 'Patrick' has to be argued for, not merely typed.
